title: ORDER BY: putting rows in a tidy line

steps.title: Sorting from small to big
steps.prompt:
A database returns rows in the order it stored them - not very helpful.
ORDER BY fixes that. It's like putting books on a shelf by height.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price;
hints: Start with SELECT name, price FROM products.
Add ORDER BY after FROM products.
We want to sort by price.
Type: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price;

steps.title: Smallest first or biggest first?
steps.task: Fill the blank so the most expensive product is first.
hints: The blank comes right after price.
There's a magic word that makes it go down the ladder.
It starts with a D.
Write DESC.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price ___;

steps.title: The most expensive three
steps.prompt:
Combine your two new powers: ORDER BY and DESC.
The output will read like a countdown of prices, top row = most expensive.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;
hints: Start with SELECT name, price FROM products.
Add ORDER BY price, then DESC at the end.
The first row should now be the rug worth 3356.82 MAD.
Type: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;
steps.memory_trick: DESC turns the list into a countdown.

steps.title: Fix the typo
steps.task: Fix the query so it sorts by stock.
hints: Run it first and read the error.
One word is misspelled.
ORDER BY has five letters in the first word.
Change ORDEY to ORDER.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, stock FROM products ORDER BY stock;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT name, stock FROM products ORDEY BY stock;
steps.memory_trick: Read errors like a friend: they are clues, not scoldings.

steps.title: Predict the first row
steps.prompt:
SELECT name, stock FROM products ORDER BY stock; 
starts from the smallest stock. Which product is at the TOP?
hints: There are several products with 0 stock.
Run the query to see them.
The first one is decided by the order the table stores them in.
It starts with 'Ras el Hanout…'.
steps.memory_trick: When stocks tie, the tie order isn't promised - notes to self: ORDER BY stock, name is the tidy way.
